milestones.description: Viete calls his calculus on symbols the logistic of species (logistica speciosa).

evidence.claim: Viete called his systematic theory the species logistic, art of calculation on symbols (1591).
Isagoge scan catalogued.

milestones.note: Same book as the first_statement; plays a naming role only for the term, not the field name 'algebra'.

milestones.label: Harriot's Artis analyticae praxis
milestones.work: Thomas Harriot, Artis analyticae praxis, London, 1631 (posthumous)
milestones.description: Harriot's posthumously printed algebra shows an independent English line of letter-based symbolic algebra.

evidence.claim: Executors published Artis Analyticae Praxis in 1631.
Artis analyticae praxis, 1631.

milestones.note: Only the publication is verified; independence from Viete and the notation details were not checked.

milestones.label: Descartes' convention
milestones.work: Descartes, La Geometrie, 1637
milestones.description: Later convention of early letters for knowns and late letters for unknowns replaced Viete's vowels.

evidence.claim: The convention was introduced later by Descartes in La Geometrie.
La Geometrie published in 1637 as an appendix to the Discours de la methode.

milestones.label: Opera mathematica
milestones.work: Viete, Opera mathematica, ed. van Schooten, Leiden 1646
milestones.description: Collected works gave the analytic art wide circulation.

evidence.claim: Opera Mathematica, Leiden 1646, cited in MacTutor's references.

milestones.note: Editor's name from general knowledge, not in the page read.

notes: Open: first purposeful application (Zetetica, 1593) not verified; the Isagoge scan is catalogued as 1591. Gradual predecessors (Diophantus, Cardano, Bombelli's abbreviations) were not researched. Lifespans for Descartes and van Schooten are unsourced here. Thin-record pass: read English Wikipedia (Francois Viete, Harriot, Bombelli, La Geometrie). Wikipedia notes Viete used vowels for unknowns and consonants for parameters, a choice Descartes reversed. Zetetica (1593) was searched in Open Library with no record, so first_application stays open. Descartes' La Geometrie year 1637 is confirmed by Wikipedia.

canonicalName: Viete: trigonometry applied to algebra (van Roomen's problem)

milestones.label: Viete's In artem analyticam isagoge
milestones.work: François Viète, In artem analyticam isagoge, Tours 1591
milestones.description: Viete introduces letters for unknowns and parameters, the symbolic algebra that his answer to van Roomen relies on.

evidence.claim: MacTutor places the Isagoge among Viete's main algebra publications of the early 1590s.

milestones.note: Publication year taken from the MacTutor page; no bibliographic record was found.

milestones.label: Van Roomen poses a degree-45 equation
milestones.work: Adriaan van Roomen, Ideae mathematicae pars prima, 1593
milestones.description: Public challenge to mathematicians.

evidence.claim: Roomen proposed the problem in 1593.
1593 book scan.

milestones.note: Whether the problem is printed in this very volume was not checked.

milestones.label: Viete publishes his answer
milestones.work: Viete, Responsum ad problema (answer to van Roomen), 1595
milestones.description: Recognises the equation as a trigonometric identity and solves it.

evidence.claim: Viete solved it by seeing an underlying trigonometric relation; answer published 1595.

milestones.note: Title of the 1595 answer is not in the page read; no bibliographic record found. Same paper plays the role of first application.

milestones.label: Trigonometry used on an algebraic equation
milestones.work: Viete's answer to van Roomen, 1595
milestones.description: First purposeful use of angle-multiplication identities to solve an algebraic equation.

evidence.claim: As above.
MacTutor notes Viete knew formulas for sin nx.

milestones.note: Same work as previous; 'first' not verified.

milestones.label: Ad angulares sectiones published
milestones.work: François Viète, Ad angulares sectiones theoremata, ed. Alexander Anderson, Paris 1615
milestones.description: The posthumous treatise on angle sections sets out the multiple-angle relations behind the degree-45 solution.

evidence.claim: MacTutor lists Viete's posthumous work on angular sections edited by Anderson.

milestones.note: Year of the posthumous edition not confirmed in a bibliographic record; the earlier note in this file also left it open.

milestones.label: Collected Opera mathematica of Viete
milestones.work: Francois Viete, Francisci Vietae Opera mathematica, 1646
milestones.description: Collected edition of Viete's mathematical works, which brings together the trigonometric-algebra material of the event.

evidence.claim: Open Library record of the 1646 Opera mathematica of Viete.

milestones.note: Editor of the 1646 edition not checked; the year is from the catalogue record.

notes: Open: Viete's later Ad angulares sectiones (posthumous, translation named on MacTutor) and its date were not verified. Zbmath: Bockstaele 2009 (1207.01007) on van Roomen. Lifespans unsourced here. No naming or institution milestone. English Wikipedia could not be read in this pass (API returned rate-limit errors for every request), so the source-first step used MacTutor biographies and history topics only. Thin pass 2: only two further milestones (Isagoge 1591, Ad angulares sectiones 1615) could be added from MacTutor; both are history-page only. Searches of zbMATH for Viete, Ad angulares sectiones and van Roomen, Ideae mathematicae returned no record, and the archive.org search for the title returned none. No naming or institution milestone exists; the history is short for this event. Re-checked MacTutor Viete in this pass: the reply to van Roomen is published 1595. No dated record of the posthumous Ad angulares sectiones (1615) was found; the Internet Archive copies located are Schooten's 1646 Opera and Viete's De aequationum recognitione (1615), a different work, so the 1615 date stays unresolved.
